Job Description

This is a 50% FTE fixed term position through July 30, 2029.

Budgeted Pay Rate

The expected pay rate for this position is $35.00 per hour at 50% FTE.

The Office for Religious & Spiritual Life (ORSL) seeks a Project Coordinator who will be part of our diverse ORSL team which supports the Stanford community by offering an array of year-round religious and spiritual events and programs. The position requires an understanding of, and commitment to, the mission and purpose of the Office for Religious & Spiritual Life, which is to oversee the religious and spiritual life of the campus, with care and compassion in not only what we do, but how we do our work for the Stanford community.

This position will provide comprehensive administrative and logistical support for projects in ORSL, including but not limited to the Design Your Spiritual Life retreat.

This role requires exceptional organizational skills, sensitivity to religious and philosophical diversity, and a deep commitment to fostering a student experience that is inclusive, reflective, and grounded in ORSL’s mission to nurture the spiritual and existential well-being of the Stanford community.

Core Duties*:

Project Coordination

Coordinate ORSL projects working across teams and functional areas to ensure timely delivery.
Coordinate weekly meetings of project teams, including scheduling, agenda preparation, note-taking, follow-up communication, and tracking action items.
Serve as primary administrative resource, providing timely support and anticipating needs related to student engagement and project planning.
Develop and maintain project timelines, task lists, and communication plans for key ORSL initiatives, programs, and events.
Regularly consult with internal and external stakeholders to determine project objectives, requirements, and outcomes, including student groups, campus partners, and program leads.

Retreat Planning & Execution

Serve as project manager for the bi-annual DYSL retreat, overseeing all logistics including transportation, lodging, meals, contracts, schedules, vendor coordination, and site requirements.
Design and maintain the full retreat timeline, coordinating with ORSL colleagues, external partners, and the teaching team to ensure a cohesive and high-quality student experience.
Coordinate procurement of supplies, equipment, and resources needed for in-class learning and contemplative practices.
In collaboration with the teaching team, contribute to the development and refinement of retreat content, activities, and learning goals.
Serve as on-site retreat coordinator, managing day-of operations, supporting student needs, and ensuring all components run smoothly and safely.

Administrative Support

Provide administrative support to the Dean for Religious & Spiritual Life, managing priorities to advance projects within the office.
Coordinate and schedule meetings with campus partners, faculty, administrators, and external stakeholders on behalf of the Dean, ensuring efficient use of the ORSL team’s time.
Arrange travel logistics for guests of the ORSL, including visiting speakers, artists, and scholars, managing itineraries, accommodations, and related correspondence.
Support the preparation and submission of annual reports, compiling data, narratives, and supporting materials from across the office.
Assist with the annual assessment process, coordinating the collection of program data, drafting summaries, and tracking timelines.
Maintain organized systems for tracking action items, deadlines, and follow-up for the Dean and the broader ORSL team.
Manage the production of agendas, meeting notes, and follow-up communications for project-related gatherings.
Other duties may be assigned.

jobs.description:

San Diego State University’s Center for Tobacco and the Environment (CTE), co-directed by Georg E. Matt, PhD, and Thomas Novotny, MD, MPH,
is an extramurally funded center established in 2022. CTE’s mission is to prevent, reduce, and eliminate the toxic legacy of environmental pollution and harm to human health caused by decades of commercial tobacco sales and use. CTE is an open, community-engaged, inter- and transdisciplinary research center that serves the diverse communities affected by the environmental impacts of commercial tobacco. CTE provides an organizational platform for the next generation of research that seeks solutions to environmental contamination and human exposure resulting from decades of tobacco use, and contributes to California’s comprehensive policy initiatives to end commercial tobacco sales and use by 2035.

CTE is home to a well-established group of multi-disciplinary scholars from different colleges at SDSU, including Sciences, Health and Human Services, Arts & Letters, and Professional Studies & Fine Arts, whose work focuses on the environmental impacts of commercial tobacco use. Researchers at CTE conduct multiple extramurally funded research projects focused on tobacco and the indoor and outdoor environment, including the Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center and the Policy Research Center for Tobacco and the Environment . Established in 2019, the mission of the Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center is to disseminate thirdhand smoke-related information to the general public, stakeholders, and tobacco control advocates. The Resource Center’s interactive website is the primary dissemination channel, supported by a robust social media presence (i.e., Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram), webinars, and print material such as newsletter articles and press releases. The Policy Research Center for Tobacco and the Environment , established in 2023, has two main policy goals (1) reduce tobacco product waste to protect the environment from microplastics pollution and chemical leaching and (2) protect indoor environments from thirdhand smoke residue. Both centers are funded by California’s Tobacco-Related Disease Research Program.

Under the general direction of CTE’s Director and Co-Directors, the Program Coordinator II will provide in-person
day-to-day oversight of Center activities, including but not limited to operations, purchasing, and budgeting; planning, implementing, and disseminating research projects; supervision of staff and interns; community outreach and education; and preparing reports for policymakers and funders.

Operations 40%

Oversee day-to-day operations of CTE, including Policy Research Center and the Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center.
Participate/prepare reports for recurring administrative team meetings.
Run regular staff meetings.
Provide supervision of direct reports and interns.
Oversee operations of (e.g., timelines, resources, deliverables) of Center projects including rapid response research projects and DIY thirdhand smoke testing services.
Support administration of expenses, purchases, and other back-office duties.
Coordinate website, social media, and other communication operations.
Support development and tracking of annual budgets.

Planning 30%

Oversee planning for and execution of all rapid response research projects, pilot projects, educational programming, community events, dissemination, outreach, resources, and other activities, including DIY testing.
Oversee community outreach and engagement, including dissemination of results to relevant policy-makers and other stakeholders.
Oversee tracking of grant milestones and goals.

Program Administration 20%

Plan and coordinate recurring events such as the Community Advisory Board and Scientific Advisory Committee.
Plan and coordinate community events such as educational webinars and town hall meetings with policymakers.
Oversee other program planning necessary for the implementation of research projects, such as IRB applications and preparation of community meetings.

Other Duties as Assigned10%

Other responsibilities as assigned by the Center Director.

Required Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and/or equivalent training and administration work experience involving study, analysis, and/or evaluation leading to the development or improvement of administrative policies, procedures, practices, or programs.
Six years of progressively responsible experience in office or administrative environment

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s, DPH, or PhD in relevant field (e.g., psychology, public or environmental health).
Knowledge of environmental and health harms of commercial tobacco.
Experience in tobacco prevention or advocacy.
Experience running multiple research, evaluation, or service projects.

San Diego State University’s Center for Tobacco and the Environment (CTE), co-directed by Georg E. Matt, PhD, and Thomas Novotny, MD, MPH,
is an extramurally funded center established in 2022. CTE’s mission is to prevent, reduce, and eliminate the toxic legacy of environmental pollution and harm to human health caused by decades of commercial tobacco sales and use. CTE is an open, community-engaged, inter- and transdisciplinary research center that serves the diverse communities affected by the environmental impacts of commercial tobacco. CTE provides an organizational platform for the next generation of research that seeks solutions to environmental contamination and human exposure resulting from decades of tobacco use, and contributes to California’s comprehensive policy initiatives to end commercial tobacco sales and use by 2035.

CTE is home to a well-established group of multi-disciplinary scholars from different colleges at SDSU, including Sciences, Health and Human Services, Arts & Letters, and Professional Studies & Fine Arts, whose work focuses on the environmental impacts of commercial tobacco use. Researchers at CTE conduct multiple extramurally funded research projects focused on tobacco and the indoor and outdoor environment, including the Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center and the Policy Research Center for Tobacco and the Environment . Established in 2019, the mission of the Thirdhand Smoke Resource Center is to disseminate thirdhand smoke-related information to the general public, stakeholders, and tobacco control advocates. The Resource Center’s interactive website is the primary dissemination channel, supported by a robust social media presence (i.e., Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram), webinars, and print material such as newsletter articles and press releases. The Policy Research Center for Tobacco and the Environment , established in 2023, has two main policy goals (1) reduce tobacco product waste to protect the environment from microplastics pollution and chemical leaching and (2) protect indoor environments from thirdhand smoke residue. Both centers are funded by California’s Tobacco-Related Disease Research Program.
